title: The Feast of Purim

questions.question: On what day was the king’s command executed?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:1 (ESV): "Now in the twelfth month... on the thirteenth day of the same..."

questions.question: What was the outcome of the day?
options: The Jews got the mastery over those who hated them
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews got the mastery over those who hated them
questions.explanation: Esther 9:1 (ESV): "...the reverse occurred: the Jews got the mastery over those who hated them."

questions.question: Why did no one stand against the Jews?
options: For the fear of them had fallen on all peoples
questions.correctAnswer: For the fear of them had fallen on all peoples
questions.explanation: Esther 9:2 (ESV): "...and no one could make a stand against them, for the fear of them had fallen on all peoples."

questions.question: How many men did the Jews kill in Susa the citadel?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:6 (ESV): "In Susa the citadel the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men."

questions.question: What happened to Haman’s ten sons?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10, 14 (ESV): "they killed the ten sons of Haman... they hanged Haman's ten sons."

questions.question: What did Esther ask for on the second day?
options: To let the Jews in Susa do tomorrow also according to this day's edict
questions.correctAnswer: To let the Jews in Susa do tomorrow also according to this day's edict
questions.explanation: Esther 9:13 (ESV): "...let the Jews who are in Susa be allowed to do tomorrow also as they have done today..."

questions.question: How many enemies were killed in the rest of the king’s provinces?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:16 (ESV): "...and killed 75,000 of those who hated them..."

questions.question: Did the Jews take any plunder?
options: No, they laid no hands on the plunder
questions.correctAnswer: No, they laid no hands on the plunder
questions.explanation: Esther 9:10, 15, 16 (ESV): "...but they laid no hands on the plunder."

questions.question: What days were established as days of feasting and gladness?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:21 (ESV): "...that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar and also the fifteenth day..."

questions.question: What is the name of this holiday?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:26 (ESV): "Therefore they called these days Purim, after the term Pur."

questions.question: What specifically were the days of Purim to be remembered for?
options: Days of feasting and gladness, days for sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Days of feasting and gladness, days for sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor
questions.explanation: Esther 9:22 (ESV): "...that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, days for sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor."

questions.question: Who wrote these things down to all the Jews?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:20 (ESV): "And Mordecai recorded these things and sent letters to all the Jews..."

questions.question: With what authority did Esther write to confirm the letter of Purim?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:29 (ESV): "Then Queen Esther... wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim."

questions.question: What was included in the ordinance regarding their fasting and lamenting?
options: Matters of their fasting and their lamenting
questions.correctAnswer: Matters of their fasting and their lamenting
questions.explanation: Esther 9:31 (ESV): "...and as they had committed themselves and their offspring in the matter of the fasts and their lamenting."

questions.question: Where was the command of Esther recorded?
questions.explanation: Esther 9:32 (ESV): "The command of Queen Esther confirmed these practices of Purim, and it was recorded in writing."

key_verse_text: As the days on which the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month that had been turned for them from sorrow into gladness and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, days for sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor.
